The text uses the word 'בְּחִינוֹת' once (paragraph 2), in the phrase 'אַרְבַּע בְּחִינוֹת', referring to the four verbs of Job 28:27 (רָאָה, סִפְּרָהּ, הֱכִינָהּ, חֲקָרָהּ) as four stages/aspects of God's review of Torah before revealing it. This is not a structural bechina declaration equating two distinct conceptual nodes as parallel expressions of the same underlying nature; it is the use of 'בְּחִינוֹת' in the plain sense of 'aspects' or 'stages' of a single process. No 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y' construction appears anywhere in the text, and no conceptual parallelism equating independent concept-nodes is present. The teaching is a practical-pedagogical statement about proper preparation for Torah teaching, not an ontological equation between concepts.
